summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin can use cron. The policy and crond service remained healthy after a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly root and opsadmin.
Set /etc/cron.allow ownership to root:root and permissions to 0600.
Verified root and opsadmin pass cron access control while an unlisted account is denied.
Restarted node1 once and verified its boot identity changed and cron functionality recovered.

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: Shows the exact two-entry allow-list, secure ownership and permissions, both accounts, successful access-control passage for root and opsadmin, and explicit denial for unlisted nobody.
Captures the healthy pre-restart state and original boot ID, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, running system state, active/enabled crond, preserved allow-list, and recovered access behavior.
